name: Lyo.Desktop
tagline: Hotkeys, clipboard, windows, and input for Linux and Windows desktop apps.
description: `HotkeyChord` parses a settings string such as `Ctrl+Shift+W`. `GlobalHotkeys.Create` grabs those chords on the X root window or with `RegisterHotKey`, so they fire while another window is focused. `Bind` replaces the whole set. An empty list releases every grab. Caps Lock and Num Lock do not change which chord matches. Call `GlobalHotkeys.InitializeThreading` before any other X11 use, including Avalonia startup. `DesktopClipboard` reads and writes text, and writes a PNG. `DesktopWindows` lists, finds, and raises top-level windows. `DesktopInput` moves the pointer, clicks, and sends keys. Linux uses X11 and XTest. Windows uses Win32. Wayland without `DISPLAY` can still use the clipboard tools. `X11WindowPlace` moves a mapped window when a plain configure would be dropped. `DesktopConfig.File` is the path of a JSON file under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lyo` or `%AppData%\Lyo`.
features: **Chords.** `HotkeyChord.Parse` accepts modifiers in any order. A single-letter key is stored in upper case. `ToString` writes Ctrl, Shift, Alt, then Meta.
**Grab.** `IGlobalHotkeys.Bind` replaces the grabbed chords. The same chord cannot appear twice. A chord another program already owns throws. The message is that the shortcut is already in use.

**Clipboard.** `DesktopClipboard.SetTextAsync` prefers `wl-copy`, then `xclip`, then `xsel`. Windows writes with `clip.exe` and reads with Win32. `SetPngAsync` offers `image/png` on Linux and a bitmap on Windows.
**Windows.** `DesktopWindows.List` returns top-level windows. `Find` matches a title substring and skips a blank title. `Activate` raises the window. An id of 0 throws.
**Input.** `DesktopInput.Click` moves, presses, and releases. `Send` types text or one chord. Modifiers go down first and come up last.
**Place.** `X11WindowPlace.TryPlace` sends `_NET_MOVERESIZE_WINDOW`. A width or height of 0 leaves that axis alone. `HasTitleBar` reads `_NET_FRAME_EXTENTS`.

**Config.** `DesktopConfig.File("screenshot.json")` is `%AppData%\Lyo\screenshot.json` on Windows. Elsewhere it is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/lyo/screenshot.json`, or `~/.config/lyo/screenshot.json` when that variable is unset.
